headline: When to Call a Contractor for Custom Shower Niche Installation
articleBody:
A recessed shower niche seems straightforward, but behind that tile sits a complex assembly of framing, plumbing, and moisture barriers. If structural elements or water management are compromised, serious hidden damage can follow.

Signs It Is Time to Call a Professional:
- You want a wide or tall niche that requires cutting into load-bearing or structural wall studs.
- In-wall plumbing pipes, vent stacks, or electrical wiring run directly through your intended installation area.
- You notice water pooling along an existing niche sill, damp drywall outside the shower, or soft spots in adjoining walls.
- You are incorporating built-in accent lighting or specialty niches that demand strict moisture protection standards.
- You are unsure how to create an unbroken waterproofing bond between the niche insert and the shower wall board.

When Professional Guidance Helps
Tying a niche into a custom tile shower requires precise trade coordination. A licensed contractor ensures wall framing stays structurally sound while maintaining complete waterproofing integrity across every corner and seam. Hidden leaks behind tiled walls can quietly rot subfloors and framing over time.
